newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT ENDS LOWER ON WEAKER US GASOLINE, IRAQ.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT ENDS LOWER ON WEAKER US GASOLINE, IRAQ.

text.p: IPE Brent futures ended weaker on Thursday just off a new intra-day low reached on the back of a battered NYMEX gasoline, after expectations of Iraqi oil exports soon weighed on the London market in early trade, brokers said.
September Brent ended the day 35 cents down at $18.85 a barrel, or five cents higher than the fresh low of $18.80 a barrel hit about 10 minutes before the close of trading.
"We were following New York which came off on the weakness in the NYMEX gasoline which got absolutely hammered down to 63.75 (cents a gallon)," a broker said.

"I'm quiet surprised it (Brent) ended this much lower. I don't know what's the story for tomorrow, I did not expect it to be so week tonight. Newswise I have not seen much to support the decline," he added.

September Brent fell to $18.95 about an hour before the close, or seven cents off the mid-day low of $18.88, as NYMEX gasoline began to slip. But it began cutting the losses as buying kicked in, climbing to about $19.06, before reversing the pattern just before the close.
Traders said the Iraqi news and talk of the award of crude export contracts by Baghdad to oil companies continued to weigh on the market somewhat.
"This talk about the Iraqi contracts has weakened it (Brent) a little bit...But in the end it does not really matter who they award the contracts to and the oil will go on the market," a broker said.
Iraq on Thursday snubbed British oil companies as Baghdad made clear it would favour "friendly" nations in awarding export contracts under the second phase of the United Nations oil-for-food deal.

Traders say Iraq will have to resume exports at a maximum capacity of 1.8 million barrels per day (bpd) in order to achieve by early September the interim $1 billion target. Iraq is allowed total sales of $2 billion under each 180-day period.
Earlier, IPE August gas oil futures closed $2.75 a tonne down at $172.50, returning to the lower range of the day's trade with little inspiration from NYMEX.
"The volume has been poor, most of it done on the spread. There was not a lot of movement in (NYMEX) heating oil to inspire any movement in gas oil," a broker said then.
